program: APPUI-01 - Windows 11 ARM64 Working App Visual Prototype

decision.design_residency: APPUI design work remains in Rylascoo/Ensemble-Website and authenticated Drive; Rylascoo/Ensemble-Project is consulted read-only for architecture/product/runtime decisions that materially affect what the app must show.
sequencing: Complete and polish the functional app UI architecture and layout.
Continue Stage/live-production rendering as the major parallel visual-design program.
After the UI framework and Stage/live-production visual system are resolved, add secondary app visual-design elements inside the established interface framework.
deferred_until_framework_is_stable: other visual programs not required for Stage or functional UI comprehension

reasoning: The Stage is the most visually complex and product-distinctive surface.
The remaining immediate design responsibility is to make the application architecture visually clean, intuitive and implementation-useful.
A single semantic UI system with Light/Dark values prevents duplicate theme-specific layouts and keeps functional meaning stable.
Keeping Stage dark in both themes preserves the current Stage authority and lets the light shell frame it as a theatrical chamber rather than forcing a second Stage art direction.

authority_boundaries.stage: PKT-STAGE-CORE-02 remains authoritative; this decision does not redesign its geometry or live-production semantics.
authority_boundaries.color: No final CLR family or final palette is selected by this decision.
authority_boundaries.engineering: No WinUI/XAML/runtime/package/Store implementation authority is created.
authority_boundaries.website: Concurrent Website Sol publication work remains separate and untouched.

engineering_truth_checked.observed_boundary: E0-D remains blocked from live execution; no application UI implementation surface is opened by CURRENT_STATE.md.

next: Create APPUI Pass 02 as paired Light/Dark representative screens sharing one semantic system and the same dark Stage; recursively audit for hierarchy, clarity, accessibility/state distinction, theme parity and implementation usefulness before decorative expansion.
